newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goodman Fielder to sell European unit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goodman Fielder to sell European unit.

text.p: Australasian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Friday it would sell its European milling and baking business, Meneba NV, for slightly more than A$300 million to Dutch-based CVC Capital Partners BV.
Goodman Fielder also said it had reached agreement to buy the New Zealand milling and baking operations of Defiance Mills Ltd for NZ$48 million.
Goodman chief executive David Hearn said Goodman and CVC Capital Partners are in an advanced stage of negotiations of the European business sale and expected to conclude in early April.
Hearn said the sale price represented a small book profit, but Goodman would record a small loss after transaction costs.
The decision to sell Meneba was in line with the company's strategy to build a sound Australasian-based food business.

"We decided that Goodman Fielder could generate few synergies between our Australian and European milling and baking operations and that Meneba would require significant resources to reach its full potential," he said.

"We concluded that the best strategy is to sell Maneba to someone that could add more value to business than we could, to focus clearly on significantly improving Australasian performance and then to develop the business where we can maximise our competitive strengths."
Goodman Fielder acquired its European food business in two stages, buying Maneba in the late 1980s and a separate flour business in the early 1990s.
Hearn said the decision to buy the New Zealand milling and baking operations of Defiance Mills would allow Goodman to consolidate its market position in New Zealand.
All conditions for the purchase were expected to be met by the end of April.
Goodman Fielder would pay about NZ$40 million after balance sheet adjustments on completion and the remaining NZ$ million over three years, Hearn said.
